TASK: The assembler was loading trays onto the overhead rack at the sub assembly station. The task was underway because this is the normal running work at this station for most of the shift. Stage of the task: in process - normal running work. Method in effect: SW-402 Sub Assembly Tray Handling. The task was being performed as written. Equipment involved: Overhead tray rack at sub assembly station 2. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: Normal working order with no open maintenance items. Object handled weighed approximately 14 pounds per tray. Object size and shape: about 24 by 16 by 4 inches, rigid with a lip on each short side. The object was held as follows: gripped by the lip at each short side with both hands, wearing general purpose gloves. PPE in use: Safety glasses and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The task is performed approximately 180 trays per shift. The assembler has performed this task for about 7 months on this station. One cycle of the task consists of the following: lift a tray from the cart at waist height, raise it with both arms extended to the rack at about shoulder height, push it forward about 18 inches onto the rails, then lower the arms and turn back to the cart. Force and posture required: about 14 pounds raised with both arms extended forward, with the right elbow above shoulder height through the push onto the rails. Symptom onset: Aching across the front of the right shoulder first noticed about six weeks ago, at first only towards the end of a shift. Symptom progression: Now present through most of the shift and continuing into the evening, and worse during the first hour after each break. Recent change in the work: The rack was raised by about 4 inches during a layout change roughly two months ago, and the tray count per shift went from 140 to 180 at the same time.

MECHANISM: Motion involved: Repeated overhead reach with the right arm raised above shoulder height and the elbow extended through the push onto the rails. Repetition: one overhead push per tray, about 180 trays per shift. Force and posture: About 14 pounds of forward push per tray with the right elbow held above shoulder height throughout the movement.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The rack height and the tray count both changed about two months ago and the station has not been reassessed since. Conditions at the point of injury: nothing notable about the environment. Timing: Symptoms are worst in the last three hours of an 8 hour shift, with no overtime worked recently. The assembler had performed this task before. No known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The symptoms could have been reported when they were first noticed six weeks ago, but they were mild and were expected to settle.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: First aid at the scene: No first aid was given at the scene because the condition was reported at the end of a shift. No first aid was given at the scene. Notification: The team lead was told at the end of the shift and EHS the following morning. Reason for the delay in reporting: the aching was mild at first and was expected to settle with rest over the weekend. Scene and equipment: Nothing was secured because there was no single event or scene to preserve. Work at the location continued in a modified way. The assembler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
